newsitem.title: PANAMA: BellSouth expands Panama cellular service.
newsitem.headline: BellSouth expands Panama cellular service.

text.p: A consortium led by U.S. telecommunications company BellSouth Corp will expand cellular phone service to Panama's second largest city by the end of September, a company spokeswoman said Tuesday.
The service will be extended to Colon on the Atlantic coast some 50 miles (80 km) from Panama City "in a matter of weeks" and to the rest of the country in two years, the spokeswoman said.
The company is working on establishing a roaming service with neighboring countries by the end of the year, she said.
The service would allow customers to use their cellular phones purchased in Panama in other countries, she said.
BSC de Panama SA, a consortium headed by BellSouth, won the license to build and operate Panama's first cellular telephone network in January in a bid of $72.61 million.

BellSouth, operator of the BSC consortium, has the largest stake with 41.5 percent. Other investors are Panama's Multi Holding Corporation, a holding company of Grupo Bancomer de Panama and Guatemala's Grupo Botran.

The consortium received a 20-year license to operate Band A, one of two nationwide cellular telephone bands. The other band will be operated by state-run telephone company INTEL, currently undergoing a partial privatization process.
